The tree's notifications → `emit()` (which calls the twin, then dispatches). Built
once, so WebTreeView's memoized adapters keep their identity across updates.

members.name: #isRendering
members.description: Mirrors render-start / render-complete — also valid while the first build is still constructing the tree.

members.name: #pendingState

type.text: { expandedPaths?: string[]; selectedPaths?: string[]; checkedPaths?: string[] }

members.description: State assigned before the first build (`expandedPaths` / `selectedPaths` / `checkedPaths`), applied right after it.

members.name: reinit
members.description: First connect (or an `on:'reinit'` change — there are none): build the engine.

members.name: update
members.description:
Cosmetic/structural change — patch the live engine. Also serves as the
PUBLIC imperative `el.update(props)` method (the old API).

Sends the FULL assembled engine config on every call, exactly like the old
`_scheduleUpdate` → `treeview.update(buildConfig())` did. This matters:
`controller.updateProps` is a merge, and several derived behaviors (e.g.
`expandLevel` auto-expansion when `data` arrives) only fire when the relevant
keys are present together. A changed-keys-only partial would drop them.
Any explicit `partial` (imperative caller) is folded over the assembled config.

members.name: connect
members.description:
Activate (every connect, after any reinit()/update()): re-attach the live
resources. The tree is built once (reinit) and survives a DOM move with all
its state; build only if it doesn't exist yet.

members.name: disconnect
members.description:
Deactivate (every disconnect — a DOM move or a removal): stop ONLY the live
resources (document listeners, observers, autoUpdate, open popups). The
engine + renderer are kept, so expansion, selection, checks, focus, search
and the scroll offset survive a move (D1).

members.name: #unsubscribePageDrag
members.description: Unsubscribe from the shared page-drag tracker (set while `highlight-on-page-drag` is live).

members.name: isArmed
members.description:
True while the tree is armed (`highlight-on-page-drag` + a node is dragged over
the page + it accepts drops). Mirrors the `armed` attribute / `:state(armed)`.

members.name: #syncPageDrag
members.description:
Join / leave the shared page-drag tracker per `highlight-on-page-drag` and the
connection state (one page listener set for every instance), then re-derive
the armed state.

members.name: #syncArmed
members.description: Armed = tracking + a node drag over the page + the tree accepts drops.

members.name: destroyCallback
members.description:
Final teardown (core `destroy()`): release what `disconnect()` keeps — the
engine, renderer, search index and clipboard registration.

members.name: #treeLoggers
members.description:
The element's instance loggers for the engine / LTree / renderer, resolved
per access: `this.log` changes when the tag's logging bundle is registered
after the element was built (it is the CORE fallback before that).

members.name: #assembleConfig
members.description:
Build the tree config from the merged `this.config`: drop element-only
keys (NON_ENGINE_KEYS) via core's `engineConfig`, which **preserves `null`**
as the clear signal (SPEC §6.1 — the engine resolves it per field), then
add the event bridges and the context (this element + its rebuild-proof
controller, so every ctx / detail carries them).

The live tree after applying pending property writes (`flush()`), so
`el.prop = x; el.method()` sees `x` (core rule; NOTES #13).

item `onClick(detail)` → built-in action → `action` event. For `renderContextMenuCallback`:
`ctx.controller.activateMenuItem(entry.item, ctx, button, event)`. Resolves `false` when
cancelled; closing the menu is the caller's job.

(`sortCallback` → `orderMember` → display value, numeric-aware) or `options.compareCallback`;

rewritten (unless `isSilent`). Works with `isSortingEnabled` off too.

tree. Same rule / options / event as sortNodes.

members.description: OUTPUT (egress) transform — clean/redact `ctx.data` as a node leaves the source (copy/cut/copy-drop).

members.description: INPUT (ingress) transform — derive ids/values from `ctx.data` as a node lands (paste/copy-drop); return null to skip.

members.name: shouldDefer
members.description: Hold the first build (core, SPEC §6.3): while set when the element first connects, nothing is built and every input, callback and listener assigned meanwhile accumulates; `release()` (or removing the attribute) then builds once. Latched after the first build.

members.name: themeSource
members.description: Where this element reads its theme from instead of the page (core, SPEC §12.10): a CSS selector (nearest matching ancestor, else the first match), `'closest'` (the nearest ancestor carrying a theme signal), or (property only) an `Element`. Unset = the page.

members.name: motion
members.description: Motion level (core, SPEC §12.16): `auto` (default — follow `window.components.motion`, then a `data-motion` on the page / an ancestor), `none` (no transitions, instant scrolling), `snappy` (short) or `smooth` (longer). Sets the shared `--base-duration-*` / `--base-scroll-behavior` tokens on the element through `data-motion`; the OS reduced-motion setting always wins.

members.name: responsive
members.description: Instance responsive rules (core, SPEC §6.7): partial configs on two axes — `device` (keyed by device class `mobile` / `tablet` / `desktop`; a mouse device is `desktop` at any width) and `breakpoint` (keyed by the window-width bucket); the breakpoint entry applies first, the device entry over it (device wins). An object or a JSON attribute, e.g. `{"device":{"tablet":{"presentation":"modal"}},"breakpoint":{"mobile":{…}}}`. Beats page rules (`window.components.responsive*`) and values set on the element; never reflects. An entry of `null` ignores the page rules while it matches.

members.name: responsiveCallback
members.description: Instance computed responsive rule (core, SPEC §6.7): `(ctx) => partial config | null | undefined`, ctx `{ env, deviceClass, breakpoint, element, component, config }` (`config` = base). Runs after `responsive` (wins key by key); re-runs on environment flips, throttled viewport-width changes, rule and config changes. `null` ignores every page rule.

children and is collapsed goes through `beforeExpandCallback` first (a

state). Fires `node-expand` for every node that actually expanded (the

members.name: _gateExpand
members.description:
Run `beforeExpandCallback` for `node`, then `apply()` when allowed. A sync
hook answers synchronously (`true` applied / `false` cancelled). An async
hook marks the node pending (loading state, `isExpandPending`) and returns a
Promise; on settle the pending mark clears and `apply()` runs unless the hook
resolved `false` (a rejection was already turned into `false` by the adapter).
A request for a node that is already pending is ignored (`false`).

members.name: toggleNodeExpanded

Toggle expand/collapse for a node clicked via the toggle UI. Honors the
`shouldExpandAsAccordion` config: when expanding under accordion mode, every
expanded sibling (whose `isCollapsible` allows it) is first collapsed
in a single batch. Programmatic `expandNodes` / `expandAll` callers
bypass the accordion. Mirrors svelte-treeview Node.svelte's
toggleExpanded() flow. An expand goes through `beforeExpandCallback`;
a node whose async hook is pending ignores the toggle.
`options.isExclusive` (expand only) replaces the accordion with the
exclusive expand of `expandNodes`; `options.isSilent` fires no events.

members.description:

already holds — gives on* events and clipboard callbacks the same relational
context. Pass the live node (preferred) or just a path (e.g. a pre-removal
snapshot, where the node is gone and only the path is known). Missing

members.name: _draggedTopLevel
members.description:
The effective top-level set being dragged: when the grabbed node is part of a
same-tree multi-selection, the draggable top-level selected subtrees (the
same set the multi-drag move loop uses); otherwise just the grabbed node.
Used to populate `dragged` on the drag/drop contexts. Call BEFORE a move
mutates the selected set.

members.name: _draggedRefs
members.description:
The full top-level dragged set as NodeRefs, correct for BOTH same-tree and
cross-tree drags — the single source of `ctx.dragged` on drag start/over/drop.
Same-tree reads the live selected set (nodes resolve). Cross-tree can't see
the source's selection, so it reads the paths the source published on drag
start (getDragSet) and resolves them through the SOURCE tree (registry) — never
this one, where the same path may name a different node. Path-only refs
(node/parent null) when the source isn't reachable; falls back to the lead node
alone when no set was published (e.g. touch). Call BEFORE a move mutates the
selected set.

guarantee the lead stays (you can prune siblings but not the node under the
cursor). Descendants are KEPT — moveNodes treats an omitted descendant as a
hole. Order is preserved (= landing order). (svelte-treeview rc13)

member is added. moveNodes/duplicateNodes treat a manifest as authoritative —
a descendant PRESENT rides along, one ABSENT is a hole — so callers that just

members.name: moveNodes

type.text: { success: boolean; movedNodes: LTreeNode<T>[]; leftBehind: LTreeNode<T>[]; error?: string }

members.description:
Batch-move a COMPLETE manifest of nodes under a target, honoring "holes".
A descendant ABSENT from the manifest is left behind by re-homing it to its
moved root's OLD parent (it physically stays put). Every source is resolved to

members.name: _applyTooltip
members.description:
Create / refresh / tear down the hover-focus tooltip for a row. The direct
analog of web-multiselect's attachOptionTooltips, built on the shared core
createTooltip (portal, autoUpdate, shouldFollowCursor, data-theme inherit). Recreated
on every node update so content tracks data (rename / _rev bump); a no-op +
teardown when disabled, no callback, or empty content. Mounts into the shadow
container so it inherits the injected --wtv-tooltip-* tokens + data-theme.

members.name: _updateContextMenu
members.description:
Reflect the engine's context-menu state. The menu itself — rendering, submenus,
positioning, dismiss, keyboard — is core `openMenu()`; it opens once per
(node, point) and reports its own close back to the engine.

members.name: _closeMenu
members.description: Close the open menu without echoing it back to the engine.

members.name: _openContextMenuFromKeyboard
members.description:
Shift+F10 / the ContextMenu key: open the menu for the focused node, below its
row, with the first item focused. Returns `false` when there is no menu to open.

members.name: dropItems
members.description:
Forget the given flat-list positions: drop them from the pending queue and
remove them from the search index, so a later search can't map a hit to a
position whose node was removed (positions are the index keys).
